A_target.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a set of propositional [[Definition:Well-Formed Formula|formulas]].
If $\Gamma \vdash \phi$ in [[Definition:Natural Deduction|natural deduction]], then $\Gamma \models \phi$.
In particular $\nvdash \bot$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\map P D$ be a property of derivations.
If $\map P D$ holds for one-line derivations consisting of an assumption, and is preserved by every inference rule, then $\map P D$ holds for every derivation.

substitutions.the property P: every valuation satisfying the open assumptions satisfies the conclusion

object_map.reformulation: Induct over derivations, checking that every rule preserves semantic consequence.

validity_conditions: Each rule must be checked against every valuation, including the discharge of assumptions.
Soundness gives consistency, since no valuation satisfies the falsum.
proof_plan: Proceed by induction on derivations, using the source result.
An assumption $\phi \in \Gamma$ is satisfied by every valuation satisfying $\Gamma$.

Each rule preserves consequence: for example, if $\Gamma, \phi \models \psi$ then $\Gamma \models \phi \to \psi$; if $\Gamma, \phi \models \chi$, $\Gamma, \psi \models \chi$ and $\Gamma \models \phi \lor \psi$, then $\Gamma \models \chi$, by cases on the valuation; and if $\Gamma, \neg \phi \models \bot$ then $\Gamma \models \phi$.
